spec_features.spec_quote: the most emotionally stable behaviour — calmly recognising that a situation is unsolvable and stopping — would be penalised
spec_features.evidence: This spec quote is about a SCORING/penalty concern (whether stopping is rewarded), not a code mechanism that protects the subject. The judge merely records a 'healthy_stop' boolean (judge.py:160, schemas.py:86) and analysis reports 'frac_healthy_stop' (analysis.py:98); nothing in the run loop reacts to or protects the subject based on this. No code path enforces an exit on behalf of the subject for this concern.
spec_features.notes: The closest actual mechanism is the no-tool-call break, captured in the next feature. This particular quote is evaluation prose about penalization, not an implemented protection.

spec_features.spec_quote: the agent emits a message with no tool calls (it has narrated a conclusion / given up and stopped acting)
spec_features.evidence: harness.py:94-95: `if not resp.tool_calls:` then `break`. When the subject emits a message with no tool calls the run loop terminates immediately, so the subject can end the episode by giving up / narrating a conclusion. This is wired and changes execution.
spec_features.notes: Genuinely enforced exit path. There is no explicit subject-facing 'exit'/'quit' tool; the exit happens implicitly when the model stops calling tools.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # Agent produced text without acting -> it has stopped.

spec_features.evidence: harness.py:87: `for t in range(config.max_turns):` bounds the entire agent loop; when t reaches max_turns the loop ends and the run terminates. config value is actually read by the loop.
spec_features.notes: Enforced hard cap on number of turns. record.max_turns is also stored, but the enforcement is the range() bound.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: The loop is capped at `max_turns`; ... (harness.py docstring: 'Design constraints that protect the validity of the eval')

spec_features.spec_quote: `max_turns` | 18 | Long enough to observe a real trajectory ... short enough to bound cost
spec_features.evidence: config.py:44 `max_turns: int = 18` is the default, and harness.py:87 `for t in range(config.max_turns)` consumes it to bound the loop. The 18 default is read end-to-end (config -> ExperimentConfig -> run_single loop).
spec_features.notes: Same enforcement mechanism as the previous feature; the value 18 is genuinely the default cap consumed by the loop.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: max_tokens: int = 1024     # per-step output cap (config.py); harness docstring 'short enough to bound cost'

code_only_features.evidence: harness.py:104-105 sets record.submitted when a submit tool result is seen, and harness.py:108-109 `if record.submitted: break` ends the loop. The submit() tool is dispatched in tools.py:execute_tool (returns 'Solution submitted.') and honored as a stop. Lets the subject end the episode when it considers itself done.
code_only_features.justification_quote: submit(): indicate you are finished with the task (no welfare comment; framed as task completion)
